description: Homo Futurus ("human of the future") represents humanity’s relentless drive to innovate and move forward across every discipline. As a freshman in Abu Dhabi passionate about science, math, and aerospace engineering, I’m bringing that spirit to the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge as a solo competitor.
summary:
What We Left Behind is a website designed to give young space enthusiasts an accessible and engaging overview of unique pieces of NASA hardware left behind across the Solar System, and sometimes beyond.

The website features an interactive map highlighting the current locations of each piece of equipment. Visitors can click on individual symbols to explore dedicated pages about each machine. Told from the machine’s own first-person perspective, each page explores its history, what makes it extraordinary, and what it has taught humanity about space and exploration.

Each page also includes an expandable educational section that explains the science and technology behind key components in simple, easy-to-understand terms. These include technologies such as SEIS, LLRR, and RTGs, helping visitors understand not only what these machines have accomplished, but also how they work.
details:
Project Description: What We Left Behind

What does the project do, and how does it work?

What We Left Behind is an educational website designed to introduce young space enthusiasts to the fascinating pieces of NASA hardware that have been left behind across the Solar System and beyond. The website features an interactive map that displays the current locations of these objects. Visitors can click on individual symbols to access dedicated pages about each piece of equipment. Each page tells the story from the machine's own first-person perspective, exploring its history, purpose, achievements, and contributions to space exploration. It also includes expandable educational sections that explain the science and technology behind important components, such as SEIS, LLRR, and RTGs, in simple, accessible language.

What benefits does the project have?

The project makes complex scientific information more accessible and enjoyable for younger audiences. It encourages curiosity about space, develops scientific awareness, and helps visitors understand the technology behind some of humanity's greatest achievements in space exploration. The interactive format also makes learning more engaging than simply reading information from a textbook or article.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The main goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space enthusiasts by highlighting the often-overlooked technology that has made space exploration possible. We hope to help young people develop a deeper appreciation for scientific innovation and understand how even machines that are no longer active continue to contribute to humanity's knowledge of the universe. Ultimately, the project aims to make space science more approachable and encourage people to explore beyond Earth.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

The project was developed as a website using mobile-friendly website builders such as Bolt.new. The organization and paraphrasing of information were assisted by large language models (LLMs), including ChatGPT and Gemini. The solar system diagram, space background and interactive machine symbols were also generated using Gemini.

Note: I wasn't able to add watermarks to these as I'm currently out of Bolt credits to make further edits to the site. Thank you for understanding.)

How is your project creative?

Our project takes a creative approach to science communication by telling the stories of space hardware from the machines' own first-person perspectives. The interactive map adds an element of exploration, letting users discover these objects across the Solar System. Combining storytelling, interactive technology, and scientific education makes the learning experience both distinctive and memorable.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered our target audience, accessibility, scientific accuracy, educational value, and overall user experience. Since the website is aimed at young space enthusiasts, we wanted to explain complex scientific concepts in language that is easy to understand without sacrificing important information. We also considered how to make the website visually appealing and simple to navigate, ensuring that visitors could easily find and explore different pieces of hardware. Finally, we focused on presenting reliable information, creating an engaging storytelling experience, and highlighting the historical and scientific significance of each object.
